finish: Ends at low-angled ledges with a slung tree (rappel anchor) at the top of the wall's routes, not on a named summit. MP: rappel the route, four double-rope rappels. A 2020 trip report on the neighbouring Narcos (which shares Wright-Pond's last pitch) says 'From here you can scramble to the summit' - an unnamed formation top, no height given.
approach_time: 1 to 1.5 hours from the Cutthroat Creek trailhead parking to a shoulder near the base of the wall's right side (MP area page; off-trail through woods, gaining elevation quickly)
summit_named_and_height: No. MP's area author says 'Little Liberty Bell' is just what the formation has always been called (informal). Search found no peak page (GNIS/Wikipedia/Peakbagger) for it; only MP uses the name. MP area page prints Elevation 6,263 ft at GPS 48.54975,-120.6435 - the same GPS as the Wright-Pond route page, i.e. MP's route/area pin, not a surveyed summit.

sources.fact: Trad, Alpine, 600 ft, 4 pitches, Grade III; GPS 48.54975,-120.6435; FA Wright & Pond 2009
P4 ends at low-angled ledges, tree with rappel slings; descent: rap route in four double-rope rappels
Area Elevation 6,263 ft, GPS 48.54975,-120.6435; name informal, 'all it's ever been called'
Approach: trailhead parking, no trail up through woods, reach base within one to 1.5 hours
Narcos 600ft; last pitch = Wright-Pond P4; can scramble to summit; descend Wright-Pond, 4 double raps

note: No page gives an approach gain. Our 'Summit' pin (48.54975,-120.6435, 6,263 ft) is copied from MP's route/area pin plus MP's area elevation, which is not a summit survey; the route ends at rappel ledges. Our Campsite pin's 4,500 ft matches the USFS trailhead elevation, so it is the trailhead height, not a camp. 1,312 ft one-way gain is not printed by any page opened. MP author also says he is only '99% certain' of the map location.
